_spec.purpose: The dedupe ledger. No topic repeats within 30 days.
_spec.why: A daily record that returns to the same story every week stops being a record and becomes a feed. The window is enforced in code, not remembered, because the run that most wants to repeat a topic is the run that found nothing else.
_spec.law: No other product's ledger memory is ever copied in here. The dedupe gate compares against recent history, and a sibling product's history would poison it.

entries.topic: The Texas A&M University System's VISION supercomputer, its entry on the world list at number 66, and the gap between a pair of System pages promising it to 12 universities and 8 state agencies in the FUTURE tense and its own documentation saying access is invitation-only under a controlled beta TODAY.
entries.angle: the instrument is a VERB. Both public pages say VISION will support and will be available; the machine's own docs say invitation-only, controlled beta, and publish no count of who can use it and no date for wider access. The deck's turn is a tense, not an accusation, and slides 4 and 7 carry the fairness by giving the chairman his own words and by crediting the System for publishing its own limit.
entries.angle_note: FOURTH DECK IN SEVEN BUILT ON WHAT A DOCUMENT DOES NOT SAY, and all three round 5 judges said so independently. Deck 11's own angle_note asked the next run to spend an opening move that is not an absence. This cover opens on a RANK, so the letter was met, and the spine underneath is still four printed absences (no meeting date, no researcher count, no source joining the two compound counts, no date for onboarding). dedupe_check cannot see this field and did not fail it. THE NEXT RUN SHOULD PICK A STORY WHERE SOMETHING HAPPENED, not one where a document is quiet.

entries.angle: the account is written in adjectives and publishes no measurement of the thing it tested, while the SAME government publishes a measured monthly count of people walking IN at that port and states outright that it collects no comparable data on the way out. Frame 7 is that pairing and it is the deck's spine.
entries.angle_note: FIFTH DECK IN EIGHT LEANING ON WHAT A DOCUMENT DOES NOT SAY, and deck 14's own angle_note asked this run not to. That field was read AFTER the deck was built, which is the wrong order and is this run's fault. dedupe_check cannot see angle_note and did not fail it, exactly as deck 14 predicted, so this run's Phase 17 made dedupe_check print it. In mitigation, counted rather than argued: seven of nine frames are things that HAPPENED, the cover opens on an event rather than on a silence, and the strongest frame is a document SAYING something, the Bureau of Transportation Statistics stating it collects no outbound data. THE NEXT RUN STILL OWES A DECK WHOSE SPINE IS A THING SOMEBODY DID.

entries.topic: ARPA-E's award to a University of Houston led coalition, GAMBIT, to use AI to design permanent magnets that surpass the properties of neodymium iron boron while weighing supply constraints, announced by Rice and by the University of Houston on September 1st and read on September 5th, 2026.
entries.angle: the record's own disagreement with itself. Rice puts the award at $2.9 million and the University of Houston, which leads the project, puts the same award at $2.88 million, and neither page reconciles them. Frame 8 hangs both figures from a single drilled hole at matched size and matched light and refuses to draw a difference, because the difference is a number neither page carries. The higher tag deliberately holds the SMALLER figure, so the pair cannot be read as a slope, which is what it was before a judge named it.
entries.angle_note: FOUR CONSECUTIVE RUN RECORDS ASKED FOR A DECK WHOSE SPINE IS A THING SOMEBODY DID, and deck 15's angle_note said it in capitals. This one is a grant that was awarded, a coalition that was named and a job one of its members has. Seven of nine frames are things that happened and the cover opens on matter rather than on a silence. The deck still ENDS on an absence, frame 9's empty bench, and that is the right place for one: it is the last frame rather than the spine, and the absence it states is scoped to the four announcements the frame cites, none of which names a material.
entries.topic_note: THIS FIELD READ 'without imported rare earths' AND NO CLAIM IN THE FILE SAYS SO. A scorer found the same reading on slide 6's dek, where it was a hard fail, and found it again here after the frame was fixed. A ledger field is memory, so a refuted reading left in it becomes the next run's premise. c11 gives the target against neodymium iron boron and c14 gives the goal as new materials while balancing supply constraint concerns. Boride and carbide are anion classes, rare earth is a cation class, and Nd2Fe14B is a rare earth boride, so the project's own NAME excludes nothing.

entries.topic: The Texas Advanced Computing Center closing the queues on Frontera permanently on October 1st, 2026, on a user guide that still calls it the largest cluster dedicated to open science in the United States, beside the guide for Horizon which says of itself that it is in progress and that the machine is still limited only to internal users.
entries.angle: TWO MANUALS IN TWO STATES OF REPAIR. The deck's instrument is documentation rather than a filing or a vote, because a manual is how a public machine is actually open, and the two guides belong to one center and sit in completely different states. The deck's structural law is that a document is lit exactly as far as it is written, so the unfinished guide is never warned about, it is simply less lit.
entities: The University of Texas at Austin
entries.angle_note: THE SPINE WAS A THING SOMEBODY DID AND THAT DEBT IS PAID. Four consecutive run records asked for it in capitals. The cover opens on a dated act, the closure, and seven of nine frames are things that happened or documents that say something rather than documents that are quiet. The one honest absence, frame 4, is scoped to one page and bylined to it. THE PLACE ARRIVED IN ROUND FOUR AND IT IS THE WRONG ONE. Three judges across two rounds charged the deck for naming no Texas place, and the answer given twice was that no claim carried one. The Horizon guide had it all along, in a snapshot this run fetched at 06:56, saying the machine goes in a new 20 MW data center with advanced liquid cooling in Round Rock, Texas. It is now claim c22, quoted on frame 6 in the source's own words and carried in the caption, and texan_check reports a place where it reported none. What did NOT get fixed is that Round Rock sits in Williamson County and belongs to the SUCCESSOR, while the machine this deck is about is at UT Austin in Travis County and is never located on any frame. So the deck names a place and still does not place its subject. The research lesson is to grep the snapshots already in hand before concluding a story carries no place, and the selection lesson is that a place belonging to the wrong noun answers the gate without answering the reader. A SECOND THING, and it is a dedupe blind spot rather than a craft note. Deck 14 on September 3rd was the Texas A&M VISION supercomputer whose own docs say access is invitation-only, and this is a Texas university supercomputer whose own docs say limited only to internal users. Different institution, different machine, different docket item, so dedupe_check cannot see it and did not fail it. Two judges said it reads as the same story twice in five days. The gate compares topic, entities and keywords and it does not compare INSTRUMENT, which is the field that would have caught this one.

entries.topic: Austin City Council adopting Resolution No. 20260812-017 on August 12th, 2026, which directs the City Manager to acquire, deploy and activate the kinds of parks security equipment it names, and in the same text bars that officer from considering a camera or drone system that depends upon artificial intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis.
entries.angle: THE SAME COUNCIL SPOKE TWICE ON THE SAME SUBJECT AND THE SECOND TIME IT CLOSED A DOOR THE FIRST LEFT OPEN. City Code Chapter 2-19, adopted in April, already lists artificial intelligence or machine learning tools among what is not permitted, with an exception for whatever the city's own policy allows. The August clause reaches a camera or drone in the parks, carries no exception at all, and binds a single officer for a single kind of purchase. The deck's structural device is the resolution's own page break, which falls between the words artificial and intelligence, so the reader's thumb performs it.
entities: Council Climate, Water, Environment, and Parks Committee
entries.angle_note: THE FIRST ANGLE WAS FALSE AND A JUDGE FOUND IT. It read that Chapter 2-19 merely WEIGHED artificial intelligence as a privacy assessment factor and that August turned it into a bar. Section 2-19-9 of the same ordinance, six pages past the section the run read, lists the tools among what is not permitted. The run had the whole fourteen page extraction in hand and had cited six other sections of it. The angle above is the rebuilt spine and it is what the whole instrument says. The check the run was missing is now written into the record: before a deck asserts a contrast between two instruments, sweep the FULL snapshot of BOTH for the subject noun and either claim or explicitly reject every place it appears. The same run then recorded that the agenda published no vote while the link titled Actions Taken By Council sat unopened on the page it had already fetched, so the sweep has to cover a snapshot's own links as well.

entries.topic: A quality improvement study at Houston Methodist Hospital comparing AI-estimated discharge dates from a commercial clinician-assisted tool against the hospital's own case managers, over inpatient encounters discharged between August 1st, 2023 and February 28th, 2024, published in JAMA Network Open on September 3rd, 2026.
entries.angle: THE TOOL GOT WORSE AS THE ANSWER GOT EASIER. At admission the two methods sat level on error. Nearer discharge, where the study says an accurate date counts for most in bed management, the case managers improved from 1.29 to 0.98 days of mean absolute error and the tool went the other way, 1.59 to 1.93. The deck's instrument is a peer-reviewed clinical study rather than a filing or a vote, which is new to this account, and its structural law is that the sun is declared once and every object throws from it.
entries.note: dedupe_check clean at 17 entries in the ledger over a 30 day window, nothing close. The `health-and-education` beat is 2 of the 17 decks in the window and is not the most recent.

The same typo stood in all three variety ledgers, which is what a number typed once per file rather than derived once per run buys. Found by the round 3 reader judge reading the dedupe window.

entries.topic: Texas State University's Ingram School of Engineering method for pavement condition assessment, now in a second phase the university describes as closer to statewide deployment with pixel-level detection of pavement damage. TxDOT funds it and donated the mobile research van the imagery comes off

The deck builds a single direction without hedging and then turns on c17, which says the precision of the technology often leads to inaccuracies that must be verified by pavement engineers. The record's own pavement condition score, where 70 or above is good or better, is what aims the repair money either way

entries.instrument: two peer-reviewed clinical papers, an expert panel review and a radiomics survival study
entries.topic: Radiology papers with Texas departments carrying an electronic article date of September 9th. An AJR expert panel review of pediatric artificial intelligence in radiology that names off-label use of adult-trained AI models on children among its ethical and regulatory concerns, and an AJNR machine learning analysis of MRI radiomics for survival prediction in brain metastases whose fixed model scored lower on an independent cohort than on the cohort it was built on
entries.angle: What a model fitted to a population does when it meets a different population, shown as a measurement rather than as a worry. The panel names the concern and publishes no figure for it. The second paper puts numbers on the same move in its own clinical domain and its authors call the result limited standalone discrimination
entries.angle_note: THE INSTRUMENT REPEATED AND THE GATE STILL CANNOT SEE IT. Carousel 19 shipped on 2026-09-09, four days before this one, with instrument a peer-reviewed clinical study and an angle of THE TOOL GOT WORSE AS THE ANSWER GOT EASIER. This deck is two peer-reviewed clinical studies whose frame 6 reads It did worse on the patients it had never seen. dedupe_check compares topic, entities and keywords, all of which genuinely differ, so it is correctly clean. Deck 17's angle_note already wrote in capitals that the gate does not compare INSTRUMENT, deck 19 added the field, and nothing reads it. TWO of three round 5 judges charged this deck for it independently and it is now the third occurrence. The next run either wires instrument into dedupe_check or stops pretending the field is a control. SECOND, THE SPINE IS AN ABSENCE AGAIN. Frame 7 is the declared turn and it is a printed negative, after decks 11, 14, 15 and 16 each asked the next run to stop building the spine on a silence. THIRD, AND THE ONE A READER PAID FOR: three of nine frames are the second paper and no frame says why they are there. Three reader judges asked for the bridge on frame 4 in three consecutive rounds and the run spent its rounds elsewhere. Put the connective where the detour starts.
entities: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
The University of Texas Medical Branch
entries.entities_note: Written from claims.json rather than from memory. Every name appears in a fetched quote. c26's affiliation field also names Duke University Medical Center, the University of California San Diego and Indiana University. Those names are deliberately kept OUT of the entities array, because the array is what dedupe_check compares and this deck prints none of them, so carrying them would make a future deck on any of the same institutions read as a repeat of this one. Frame 8 draws departments rather than counties because the source identifies the Texas authors by department. The record does file both items by county, Harris and Dallas for the review and Harris and Galveston for the second paper, and an earlier version of this note said it filed neither, which was false and was read back off the docket's own geography field.
keywords: off-label use of adult-trained AI models
entries.prose_note: The counts this prose could have carried are in computed.json and aggregates.json and on the frames instead. ledger_check refuses a number word in durable memory that its own vocabulary cannot re-derive.

entries.instrument: ERCOT's Verification RFI user guide v1.1, its August 20th presentation to the utility commission, market notice M-A080326-04, and a developer's release to its own shareholders
entries.topic: The eligibility verification the grid operator is running on the large loads in its interconnection queue. A Request for Information and Production issued to every conditionally classified load, due in 10 business days with a 5 day extension that may be requested, carrying a notarized attestation from the load entity, the distribution provider and the transmission provider, submittable only by the transmission provider and locked once sent. 17 large loads at 6,608 MW of modeled 5 year peak have finished every other process the grid operator runs and hold no approval to energize
entries.angle: A statewide audit ordered from the Governor's office turned out to be a form. The deck is built on the gap between the size of the order and the size of the instrument, and on the fact that the public notice about the classifications carries procedure, a control number and not a single load name
entries.angle_note: The public account of what a classification did to a named project came from a company telling its own shareholders rather than from any list, which is why frame 8 is a shareholder announcement and frame 2 is a notice that names nobody. Both are document frames and they carry opposite contents.
entries.entities_note: Dickens County is the one Texas place the record can name and it comes off the developer's own page, never off a list. No claim locates the Caspian project anywhere, so no surface joins it to a county.
entries.prose_note: dedupe_check put the nearest prior deck at 0.46, carousel no. 3 on August 19th, which was about the schedule the Governor's directive broke rather than the questionnaire it produced twenty three days later.

entries.instrument: ERCOT's Item 10 presentation to its own Board of Directors on September 14th and 15th, 2026, and PGRR 144 on the market rules site
entries.topic: The 3 emerging operational risks ERCOT put in front of its own Board for the Large Loads on its system, each with a mitigation, and the 3 mitigations at 3 different stages. The ride-through rule is in force, effective August 1st. The modeling rule reached the Board this month. The rule that would hold a Large Load's swing is not filed and carries no number, and ERCOT gives September or October for filing it. The same 6 pages say the dynamic models ERCOT uses to study these loads have proven inaccurate.
entries.angle: The deck is built on the gap between a named risk and the state of the rule meant to answer it. Every statement of harm in the document is modal, so the deck draws nothing broken anywhere in 9 frames, and the 6 pages name no data center, no company, no generator and no county.
entries.angle_note: The turn is frame 4, at the coupling, which is the metal ERCOT's word fatigue points at. It is also the frame where drawing a crack would have turned a could into a has, and the refusal to draw one is the deck's argument rather than a limitation on it.
entries.entities_note: No private party is named because the document names none. Texas A&M is the only institution in it besides the grid operator and the commission, which is what frame 8's line rests on.
entries.prose_note: Every count above is written in digits. ledger_check compares spelled-out number words against the run's own figure keys, and this run's keys are not the vocabulary that check carries.

entries.instrument: a university release read against the federal award record that funds it
entries.topic: a federally funded AI tutor built to withhold the answer, and the same method pointed at police de-escalation training
entries.angle: the same machine in a second room, paid for by a different agency
entries.angle_note: The surprising fact is not the tutor. It is that the same researcher's method is already being tested with the Fort Worth Police Department under a SEPARATE Department of Justice grant, disclosed only in a footnote, while the NSF award that pays for the classroom half had not started. TWO JUDGES THIS RUN NAMED THE SAME BLIND SPOT: the INSTRUMENT here, reading an NSF abstract against the university's own release, is the same instrument carousel 11 used eighteen days ago on a robotics award. dedupe_check compares topic, entities and keywords and all three differ, so it cannot see an instrument repeat. That is the field to watch and nothing reads it yet.
entries.entities_note: The researcher is printed as Shuchi Deb, the release's own form. The federal record calls her Shuchisnigdha Deb (c28) and the deck does not reconcile the two.
entries.prose_note: The deck never puts the university's $750,000 and the federal $749,999.00 in one frame, and never implies one grant behind both uses. The Department of Justice record for 15PBJA-23-GG-06172-NTCP was not reached this run (a4) and frame 7 draws that gap as an empty lit field rather than filling it.

entries.instrument: a corporate release read against the statute that may or may not reach it
entries.topic: an Epic-built assistant drafting the patient-facing note that comes with a lab result at a Houston health system, and a Texas disclosure statute whose reach over a private hospital the chapter does not settle
entries.angle: the statute names the duty holder differently in different subsections and the chapter never reconciles them
entries.angle_note: The finding is textual rather than numeric. Sec. 552.051(b) puts the disclosure duty on a GOVERNMENTAL AGENCY and (f) puts one on THE PROVIDER OF THE SERVICE OR TREATMENT without saying whether that provider must be governmental, and Chapter 552 has no section headed Applicability. The fact-checker REJECTED the finding that the statute requires this hospital to disclose, and the deck's hardest editorial work was honouring that rejection in the ARRANGEMENT and not only in the strings. Two rounds of judges caught it leaning anyway: round 2 found subsection (b) spliced from two non-adjacent spans with no mark (a hard fail), and round 3 found (c) truncated exactly where it stopped helping, which made an obviousness rule read as a second duty holder. Both are now set in full and the frame carries BOTH readings. THE INSTRUMENT BLIND SPOT IS RECORDED FOR THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE RUN AND IT IS NOW WORSE THAN A NOTE. Four separate round 5 judges named it independently: this is the third clinical AI deck in nine days (no. 19 September 9th, no. 23 September 13th, this one), the second Houston hospital in nine, and the instrument, a corporate release read against an official record, is what no. 26 shipped ONE DAY EARLIER. dedupe_check compares topic, entities and keywords and all three genuinely differ, so it is clean and it is clean about the wrong thing. Decks 17, 19, 23 and 26 each wrote this field; nothing reads it.
entries.entities_note: UC San Diego Health appears only inside frame 6's image as a locator, because the 52 doctors are a California pilot of a DIFFERENT feature (draft replies to patient messages, not result notes) and c14's note forbids presenting it as a test of the same thing. Three reader judges over three rounds asked for the bridge before the hook and dek carried it.
entries.prose_note: The deck never says the hospital must disclose or is in violation, on any frame, in the caption, or cumulatively across the 4-7-8-9 run, which two integrity judges checked explicitly. Frame 7 prints the reading that cuts AGAINST the deck in its own type. The one thing it still does not print is (f)'s opening trigger clause, which is what makes (f) the health care provision, and a round 5 judge named that as an omission rather than a falsehood. It is the first item for the next run.

entries.instrument: three agendas of one public body read against that same body's own minutes archive
entries.topic: Hays County put a machine that writes police reports and a machine that writes the court's own minutes on its September agendas, and published no disposition for any of them
entries.angle: a single county reaching opposite postures toward machines that write official records, inside a fortnight, with no outcome on the public record for either
entries.angle_note: THE COUNTS THIS PROSE USED TO STATE NOW LIVE IN figures.json AND NOWHERE ELSE, and the reason is a gate limitation worth knowing. ledger_check.check_topics validates every number word in the newest topic and angle against figures.json, but only for keys in COUNTING_FIGURES, which is a fixed tuple of one earlier deck's domain names: restricted_count, declined_count, stated_binding and so on. A deck whose figures are september_agendas and documents_behind_the_deck computes an empty allowed set, so every number word it writes fails. The counts were real and computed. They are in figures.json, in the deck and in the run record, and this prose now carries none, which is the one thing that cannot go stale. The gate's fixed key list is in the upgrade backlog. THE INSTRUMENT BREAKS A STREAK AND THE SPINE REPEATS ONE. A county commissioners court agenda read straight off the county's portal is an instrument this product had not used, and the round-5 reader judge checked it against nos. 23, 25, 26 and 27 and called it the first local-government primary-document deck in the window. That is the blind spot five consecutive run records flagged, and it is broken here. What did NOT change is the spine: the declared turn is an absence again, the cover's own dek is an absence, and the caption closes on one. Decks 11, 14, 15, 16 and 23 each asked in capitals for a deck whose spine is a thing somebody DID. This is the sixth. Two judges counted six of nine frames as things that happened, so the absences bracket rather than carry, and they still occupy the cover and the close, which are the two surfaces a feed reader sees. FRAME 7 IS THE FOURTH TEXAS COUNTY MESH IN SIX DECKS (23, 24, 25) and carousel 1 CUT this exact frame on 2026-08-16 after three independent reviews called it the most cuttable in the deck. Both readers would cut it. It shipped because round 5 is the cap and three earlier art repairs each introduced a defect the next round caught.
entries.entities_note: Tyler Technologies is named on frame 6 only because the round-2 integrity judge showed that withholding it while printing the adjacency invited the Axon comparison the fact checker rejected by name. Naming it makes the frame's disclaimer cover the pair a reader is actually joining. Four commissioners are named on frames 2 and 4 from c5 and c10, verbatim and quoted, after three rounds found nine frames naming no human being.
entries.prose_note: No frame, and no line of the caption, says the court decided, approved, rejected or tabled anything. The fact checker rejected 'the Court gave opposite answers' by name and the deck honours it in the ARRANGEMENT as well as the strings: the two page frames are drawn at different distances and opposite rotations so they can never read as a before and an after. Three integrity judges checked it explicitly across six rounds and none found a disposition asserted. WHAT THE DECK DOES NOT GIVE A READER IS A NEXT STEP, and the reason is recorded rather than papered over: this run fetched no page stating when the court next meets. One fetch of the body's own landing page would have returned the day, the hour and the address. It fetched the minutes archive on that same domain and never asked for it.

entries.instrument: one state press release and one grid operator market notice issued the same day, read against the statute each of them names
entries.topic: The Office of the Texas Governor directed the Texas Water Development Board to enforce the state water use survey against data centers, naming a criminal offense and a TCEQ permit ineligibility that the Texas Water Code already carried, and ERCOT issued a market notice the same day carrying the board's own water questions to data center developers with a response deadline and a notarized attestation requirement.
entries.angle: The law did not change and the enforcement did. Every consequence in the directive is a consequence that was already on the books, so the deck draws no legislature, no new rule and nothing having happened yet, and its argument is the gap between a dormant penalty and a penalty switched on.
entries.angle_note: THE DECK CARRIES NO PLACE AND KNEW IT AT SELECTION. `texan_check` read places NONE on the story before a frame was planned, which is what the gate is for, so the run planned to carry the score on art and on the closing frame instead of learning it from a judge in a late round. THE INSTRUMENT IS THE FIFTH ERCOT REQUEST IN THE WINDOW and a round 1 judge said so plainly. `c18` separates this notice from the Batch Zero request by name, in the notice's own words, and that sentence is printed on no frame. `dedupe_check` compares entities and keywords and can't see an INSTRUMENT repeat, which four earlier run records have each written in capitals. This is the fifth.
entries.entities_note: No private party is named because neither document names one. The Governor's office asserts that major water users appear to have committed violations and names no company, no county and no volume.
entries.prose_note: Every count above is written in words that are not number words, because `ledger_check` validates spelled number words in the newest topic against this run's own figure keys and this run writes no figures.json.

entries.instrument: one federal award record read through the funder's own search API, plus three counts read from a federal regulator's public query interface
entries.topic: The National Science Foundation made a standard grant to the Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station for AI enabled predictive digital twins of freshwater infrastructure under cascading hazards, with the abstract's first stated direction aimed at small and mid sized systems, against an EPA Envirofacts count of the active community water systems in Texas and of how many of them are small.
entries.angle: The award's own abstract states the criticism, so the deck hands the reader that sentence rather than paraphrasing it, and the criticism is narrow. It is about instruments and not about people. Nothing is deployed, the award's verb is the conditional, and the deck's argument is the distance between a record that is complete and a question a complete record cannot answer.
entries.angle_note: THE STRONGEST STORY OF THE DAY WAS REFUSED ON THE GATE AND IT IS WORTH THE LINE. The Flock split, El Paso ordering removal while Carrollton expanded the same night and TxDOT suspending permits above both, returned dedupe_check LIKELY REPEAT at 0.74 against carousel no. 12 of August 30th. The full entry was read rather than its title, as the phase requires, and it is a repeat. runs/carousel/2026-09-20/SELECTION.md carries the reasoning. THE DECK CARRIES NO PLACE AND THREE JUDGES SAID SO ACROSS TWO ROUNDS. Brazos County is the drawn world and reaches no frame, and the deck's own law forbids a county sign in the drawing. Nothing forbade the copy from placing it, and that is a cost this run took rather than a rule it obeyed.
entries.entities_note: The principal investigator is named in the record and appears on ONE surface, frame 3's reproduction of the award record's own identifying fields, where the line reads 'pi  Sudipta Chowdhury' and traces to c3. An earlier draft of this note said the name is on no frame, which was wrong, and a round 4 reader judge caught it against the pixels. No frame carries the name in its own voice: the deck does not put a person in a headline or a dek, because the abstract's criticism is explicitly about instruments rather than about anybody's practice, and reproducing a public award record's field list is a different act from making a person the subject.

entries.instrument: one city council briefing PDF read from the city's own document server, plus a September 8th city manager memo that is published at NO city URL and reaches the record only through two broadcast outlets quoting it
entries.topic: The City of Dallas put 100 AI enabled cameras on its sanitation brush trucks under a contract put to the Finance Committee on December 9th, 2025, has issued its first code citations from what those cameras detected, and sends what it calls courtesy notices to property owners. The December briefing set out its refusals in the document's own words. Whether the city kept them is NOT something this record establishes. FOX 4 reports the memo saying citations issue only after an in-person inspection, NBC 5 reports what the city says its cameras and humans did, and nothing among 51 claims has anybody addressing NOT staff replacement at all.
entries.angle: The record does not establish that the city broke a promise, and it does not establish that the city kept its promises either. What it carries is the city's own account of its own process, and the friction is entirely in a letter. A memo says a courtesy notice is not a warning or a violation. The notice itself carries violations identified in bold, tells the owner what the City may do if the violations remain, and asks them to correct promptly to avoid further enforcement action. Asked the plain question, the assistant director of Code Compliance said you could call that a warning.
entries.angle_note: NOT an accusation, and NOT a finding of compliance either. THIS IS THE ONE THING THE NEXT RUN MUST NOT INHERIT WRONG. An earlier cut of this entry said the city 'has kept all three' and that 'the December promises were KEPT', and an integrity judge called it a hard fail on the caption that carried the same sentence. Nothing fetched supports it. c44 is FOX 4 reporting what the memo SAYS about the city's own process, and c44's own text ends 'reported as kept'. c17 is NBC 5 reporting violations 'that the city says AI cameras first detected and humans later confirmed'. Both are the city describing itself and neither is an audit. The deck spends four frames showing that the city's self-description of its NOTICE is contradicted by the notice's own text, so accepting its self-description of its CITATION PROCESS without attribution was the same error the deck exists to point at.
entries.entities_note: Morrison is a private homeowner who spoke to NBC 5 on the record. No address is drawn or named anywhere in nine frames and no drawn building can be read as one real property, which is why the mute world law is in the chassis.
entries.prose_note: The nearest recent neighbours in the record are plate reader stories, tx-2026-0180 Leander and tx-2026-0174 El Paso, and this is not one. No plate reader, no police department, no law enforcement database, and the detected thing is a roof and a kerb rather than a vehicle. dedupe_check cleared it. AND THE DEDUPE NOTE MISSED ITS NEAREST NEIGHBOUR, which a judge caught. Carousel no. 18 on 2026-09-08, thirteen days back, is Austin barring its city manager from buying park cameras or drones that depend on artificial intelligence: a Texas city government, AI, and cameras pointed at residents. This entry checked itself against the plate reader items in Leander and El Paso and never named no. 18. It is still not a repeat, on mechanism and on decision: Austin is a council restricting a future purchase and this is a department already sending letters. But six earlier entries wrote the dedupe blind spot into this ledger in capitals and this one had to be told.

entries.instrument: three Office of the Governor releases read from gov.texas.gov, one TCEQ hearing cancellation notice read from the agency's own decisions page, and two first party company releases, the Kodiak supply agreement and the New Era Energy PPA carried on GlobeNewswire. No journalism claim carries a figure on any frame.
entries.topic: A September 21st directive tells TCEQ to issue no permits SOUGHT BY data centers until the ERCOT interconnection audit is done, and tells the agency to align its permitting decisions with what the audits find. The halt is scoped by who is asking. The audit it waits on is scoped by what is advancing through the interconnection process. A West Texas site contracting 76 megawatts behind the meter from about 40 reciprocating gas engines never enters that process, so the audit produces nothing for a permit reviewer to align to. The separate water board directive states a CONSEQUENCE, that a data center failing to return the survey is ineligible for TCEQ permits under the Water Code chapter it names, and it states nothing about which data centers receive the survey. THAT DISTINCTION COST THIS RUN A HARD FAIL AND IS WRITTEN HERE SO THE NEXT RUN INHERITS THE NARROW READING AND NOT THE WIDE.
entries.angle: the scope of the halt set beside the scope of the audit it waits on, read as a gap a real project already sits in
entries.what_was_refused: The air permit MECHANISM. The original argument was that behind the meter engines need a New Source Review air permit and that this is the instrument the halt actually reaches. Verification could not establish it: the agency's own guidance pages (c14, c15) describe engines as the kind of facility found at sources needing NSR and say nothing about whether or when a particular installation is one. The deck states the two scopes and stops, and the web edition says in its own section that no mechanism is asserted.
entries.angle_note: THIS IS THE THIRD DECK IN TEN DAYS BUILT ON A GOVERNOR'S OFFICE DIRECTIVE TO A STATE AGENCY ABOUT DATA CENTERS, after no. 24 on September 14th and no. 29 on September 19th, and dedupe_check returned LIKELY REPEAT at 0.72 against no. 29. The override is recorded in SELECTION.md with its reasons: a different agency, a different instrument, a different docket item and an argument that is different in kind. One round 1 scorer called it a hard fail anyway and stated the counter-argument themselves, which is the honest way to disagree and is why it is written here rather than left in a scoring card. THE NEXT RUN SHOULD TREAT A FOURTH GOVERNOR DIRECTIVE AS A REPEAT WHATEVER THE KEYWORDS SAY. The entry also shipped without a `keywords` array on its first write, which is one of the three fields dedupe_check compares, so the run made itself harder for the next run to see in the run where it sat closest to a repeat it has been. That is the fifth instrument repeat this ledger records in capitals.
